paper_metadata.title: Nitrogen-induced hardening of refractory high entropy alloys containing laminar ordered phases

evidence.quote: One class of materials that show promise are refractory high entropy alloys (RHEAs) [1–3] . Comprised of four or more refractory elements (e.g. Hf, Mo, Nb, Ta, Ti, V, W, Zr) ranging in concentrations between 5-35 at.%, RHEAs have been shown to exhibit strengths in excess of 400 MPa at temperatures up to 1600 °C [4–6].
The main goal of this work was to develop refractory HEAs that contain coherent nitride phases in order to maximize hardness.

the equiaxed C-N-Nb-Ta-rich carbonitride phase was structurally similar to the rock salt NbN crystal structure having a reported lattice parameter of a = b = c = 4.44 Å [55] . Fig. 6 d and h show VESTA projections down the [001] and [110] crystallographic directions of NbN further confirming that the crystal structure of the Nb-Ta carbonitride phase was structurally similar to NbN. It was therefore determined that the Nb and Ta atoms share lattice sites and thus the phase was identified as (Nb,Ta)2CN.
